```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
library(vellumwidget)
library(igraph)
```

A transfer window is a network. Players move from club to club, and the 18
Bundesliga clubs trade with each other, with the lower German leagues, and with
clubs across Europe and beyond. This page draws the summer 2025 window that way,
with one extra question on every node: how did those players move? For cash, on
loan, back from a loan, or on a free?

The data was scraped from
[transfermarkt.com](https://www.transfermarkt.com/bundesliga/transfers/wettbewerb/L1/saison_id/2025)'s
Bundesliga transfer page for the 2025/26 season: 645 arrivals and departures,
each with player, origin, destination and fee. Clubs outside the Bundesliga are
already collapsed to their country, so "England" stands for every English club
and "Germany" for the German clubs below the top flight. The file is committed
as `data/bundesliga-transfers-2025.csv`.

```{r}
tr <- read.csv("data/bundesliga-transfers-2025.csv")
# Retirements and players leaving for no club are not moves between two clubs.
tr <- tr[!tr$from %in% c("Retired", "Without Club") &
         !tr$to %in% c("Retired", "Without Club"), ]

# Five kinds of deal, read off the fee column.
tr$type <- ifelse(grepl("^End of loan", tr$fee), "loan_return",
           ifelse(grepl("loan", tr$fee, ignore.case = TRUE), "loan",
           ifelse(grepl("^free", tr$fee), "free",
           ifelse(grepl("€", tr$fee), "fee", "other"))))
table(tr$type)
```

"Other" is a fee column of `-` or `?`: mostly youth players promoted from a
club's own academy and deals whose terms were not published.

```{r}
short <- c(
  "1.FC Heidenheim 1846" = "Heidenheim", "1.FC Köln" = "Köln",
  "1.FC Union Berlin" = "Union Berlin", "1.FSV Mainz 05" = "Mainz",
  "Bayer 04 Leverkusen" = "Leverkusen", "Bayern Munich" = "Bayern",
  "Borussia Dortmund" = "Dortmund", "Borussia Mönchengladbach" = "Gladbach",
  "Eintracht Frankfurt" = "Frankfurt", "FC Augsburg" = "Augsburg",
  "FC St. Pauli" = "St. Pauli", "Hamburger SV" = "Hamburg",
  "RB Leipzig" = "Leipzig", "SC Freiburg" = "Freiburg",
  "SV Werder Bremen" = "Bremen", "TSG 1899 Hoffenheim" = "Hoffenheim",
  "VfB Stuttgart" = "Stuttgart", "VfL Wolfsburg" = "Wolfsburg"
)
rename <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(short), short[x], x)
tr$from <- rename(tr$from)
tr$to <- rename(tr$to)

# Nodes: each club or country, with its deals counted by type (both directions).
types <- c("fee", "loan", "loan_return", "free", "other")
ends <- rbind(data.frame(name = tr$from, type = tr$type),
              data.frame(name = tr$to, type = tr$type))
counts <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(ends$name, factor(ends$type, levels = types)))
nodes <- data.frame(name = rownames(counts), counts, row.names = NULL)
nodes$kind <- ifelse(nodes$name %in% short, "club", "abroad")

# Edges: one per pair of clubs that traded, weighted by the number of players.
edges <- aggregate(list(n = rep(1, nrow(tr))), tr[c("from", "to")], sum)
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, vertices = nodes, directed = TRUE)
c(nodes = vcount(g), edges = ecount(g))
```

## The layout

A force layout of this graph is a hairball: every club trades with Germany and
England, so they get pulled to the middle and everything piles up around them.
A layout with two rings reads better. The 18 clubs go on an inner circle, in the
order a Kamada–Kawai layout of the club-to-club deals puts them, so clubs that
trade with each other sit side by side. Every country goes on an outer ring at
the average angle of the clubs it dealt with. `vgraph()` takes the resulting
coordinate matrix as its `layout`.

```{r}
und <- as_undirected(g, mode = "collapse")
club <- V(g)$kind == "club"

kk <- layout_with_kk(induced_subgraph(und, which(club)))
ang <- numeric(vcount(g))
ang[which(club)[order(atan2(kk[, 2] - mean(kk[, 2]), kk[, 1] - mean(kk[, 1])))]] <-
  seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = sum(club) + 1)[-1]

for (v in which(!club)) {
  nb <- intersect(as.integer(neighbors(und, v)), which(club))
  ang[v] <- atan2(mean(sin(ang[nb])), mean(cos(ang[nb])))
}
# then spread the outer ring evenly, keeping that order
out <- which(!club)
out <- out[order(ang[out])]
ang[out] <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = length(out) + 1)[-1] + ang[out[1]]

r <- ifelse(club, 1, 1.9)
xy <- cbind(r * cos(ang), r * sin(ang))
```

## What is drawn

- `mark_edges()` draws one line per trading pair, `linewidth = n` maps the
  number of players onto `scale_edge_width()`.
- `mark_node_pie()` replaces each node with a pie whose wedges come from the
  five count columns. It is drawn twice, from the club rows and from the country
  rows of `vgraph()`'s node table, so the clubs get larger pies.
- `mark_node_text(repel = TRUE)` nudges every label off its pie and clear of
  its neighbours, with a leader line where it had to move far.
- The pie colours are named in the subtitle with `md()` colour spans, which do
  the job of a legend.

```{r}
pal <- c(fee = "#8c2d19", loan = "#c9822b", loan_return = "#e8c77a",
         free = "#5f7f5a", other = "#b8ad99")
key <- paste0(
  "[**fee**]{", pal["fee"], "}, [**loan**]{", pal["loan"], "}, ",
  "[**loan return**]{#b8963e}, [**free**]{", pal["free"], "}, [**other**]{#8f846f}"
)

net <- vgraph(g, layout = xy, width = 8, height = 8)
clubs <- net@data[net@data$kind == "club", ]
abroad <- net@data[net@data$kind == "abroad", ]

net <- net |>
  mark_edges(color = "#6b4f2c", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = n) |>
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.3, 2.5)) |>
  mark_node_pie(cols = types, size = 2.4, fill = unname(pal), data = abroad) |>
  mark_node_pie(cols = types, size = 4.2, fill = unname(pal), data = clubs) |>
  mark_node_text(label = name, size = 7, data = abroad, color = "#5a4a32",
                 repel = TRUE, point_padding = 3, seed = 1) |>
  mark_node_text(label = name, size = 8, data = clubs, fontface = "bold",
                 repel = TRUE, point_padding = 4, seed = 1) |>
  labs(
    title = "Who traded with whom: Bundesliga transfers, summer 2025",
    subtitle = md(paste("Each pie splits a club's or a country's deals by type:", key))
  ) |>
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: "Network of Bundesliga transfers in summer 2025: 18 clubs on an inner ring and 35 countries on an outer ring, each drawn as a pie of transfer types, with lines between clubs that traded players and thicker lines for more players"
vg(net, "bundesliga-network", dpi = 130)
```

The thick bundle of lines on one side is Germany. The lower leagues are the
biggest trading partner by far, in 202 of the deals, mostly loans out, loan
returns in, and academy players moving up. England (78) and France (52) come
next. The club pies are not alike. Frankfurt, Leverkusen, Stuttgart and
Dortmund did close to half their business for a fee. At Heidenheim, Bayern and
Mainz, about 60% of the deals are loans and loan returns, so their pies are
mostly orange and yellow. Bremen paid or received a fee in 3 of its 33 deals.
On the outer ring, many countries are a single player and a single colour.

## Explore it

`select_neighbours()` adds the interaction. Hover a node and the widget lights
up the node, its edges and the clubs or countries at their other ends, and dims
everything else. Hover an edge for the pair it joins. The selection is part of
the spec, so it works on the static page with no server.

```{r}
#| column: page-inset-right
net |>
  select_neighbours(on = "hover") |>
  as_widget()
```

Try Hamburg, back in the Bundesliga: it dealt with 24 different clubs and
countries, more than anyone else. Then try Heidenheim, with 8.

The edge routing is plain straight lines. `mark_edge_bundle()` can bundle them
(see [edge bundling](network-bundle.qmd)), but on two rings force bundling bends
edges into loops around the nodes, and the straight version is easier to read.
